Citation style: author-year, per TASK.md's explicit '(FirstAuthor et al., Year)' instruction, which overrides the generic profile's default numeric style.

accepted_risks.detail: Two sources cited by project/paper.txt (ref [16] L. Moreau; ref [19] P. Torelli and M. Bangale) and one more (ref [1] TinyML foundation) list no publication year in the reference list.
accepted_risks.decision: Cite [16] as (Moreau) and [19] as (Torelli and Bangale), omitting the year rather than inventing one. Reference [1] (TinyML foundation, a URL only, no author/year) is not cited in the new paper; the term 'TinyML' is used without a formal citation, consistent with not fabricating missing bibliographic metadata.

accepted_risks.detail: corpus/source_registry.json's schema (schemas/source_registry.schema.json) requires an integer 'year' for every registered source, but refs [16] (Moreau) and [19] (Torelli and Bangale) give no year at all in project/paper.txt's reference list (see AR-005). Filling in any integer to satisfy the schema would be inventing a publication year, which the hard rules forbid outright.
accepted_risks.decision: MLMark (ref [19]) and the Moreau/Edge-Impulse project (ref [16]) are NOT given formal source_registry.json entries. They are still named in the new paper's prose exactly as the kind of thing they are (a benchmark white paper; a public development-platform project), but without a parenthetical (Author, Year) citation, since no year exists to report. claim_evidence_map.json's C004 and C031 no longer list SRC-003/SRC-017 in their 'sources' field. This keeps every registered source schema-valid without fabricating a year, and keeps every in-text citation traceable to a real reference-list entry.

accepted_risks.detail: The MLPerf Tiny paper being presented is itself first-authored by Banbury (2021), and it also cites a different Banbury et al. (2021) paper (Micronets, ref [4]).
accepted_risks.decision: The new paper never needs to self-cite the source project. Only the Micronets citation appears, as (Banbury et al., 2021); no ambiguity results.
